Absorption.description: D2: absorption parameters, one lane per formulation with its studies, and the dissolution profiles.
Absorption.title: Absorption

AcceptanceView.description: The limits of the chosen tier as the MAP records them (UNVERIFIED ruleset), and the internal target (MS-01 §8).
AcceptanceView.title: AcceptanceView

AgentChain.description:
The one-click choices, in order, an agent goes on with when its own model fails (empty: none), who set them and
why, and the notice the console shows before they are saved.
AgentChain.title: AgentChain

AgentRow.description:
One agent's model as the console sets it ("environment": the server's own configuration), and what it runs on
now (`runs_on`, the model the next run would take, or why none). `choice`: the one-click choice the setting is (its
provider and model), None for any other setting.
AgentRow.title: AgentRow

AgentRunRow.description:
One agent run on a project as Agent activity lists it (R-N05): who started it, on which model, how long, what it
used, how many tool calls the runtime refused, and the model it fell back from. No cost: that stays in the admin
console.
AgentRunRow.title: AgentRunRow

AgentsPage.description:
`efforts` and `claude_models`: the choices for an agent on Claude (Bedrock's model ids); `groq_efforts`: on
GroqCloud; `choices`: the one-click choices each agent's row offers; `chain`: what every agent goes on with when its
model fails.
AgentsPage.title: AgentsPage

AgentsStatus.description:
`agent_jobs.agents_status`: whether an LLM provider is configured (provider and model when it is); `then`: the
models it goes on with, in order, when that one fails (the admin console's chain).
AgentsStatus.title: AgentsStatus

AlternativeView.description: A source the selection did not keep (D-32): how far it stands from the kept value.
AlternativeView.title: AlternativeView

ApplicationInput.description: One input an analysis template declares (`analysis_templates.TemplateInput`) and the value the plan holds.
ApplicationInput.title: ApplicationInput

ApplicationRequest.description: An application the campaign runs at S6 (T-31): an analysis template and the person's inputs to it.
ApplicationRequest.title: ApplicationRequest

ApplicationView.description: An application code with its plain name and the data items it adds (the requirement templates).
ApplicationView.title: ApplicationView

ArchivedView.description: Who archived a project, when and why (page review 1: archived projects are hidden, never erased).
ArchivedView.title: ArchivedView

ArtifactKind.description: What a phase produces (plan §5.2). Order follows the phases.
ArtifactKind.title: ArtifactKind

AssessmentTable.description: One table per question of interest (M15 Appendix 1, footnote 1).
AssessmentTable.title: AssessmentTable

BlindingChoice.description: The MIDD lead's blinding choice for the project (D-15), with its reason.
BlindingChoice.title: BlindingChoice

BlindingView.description: `deps.blinding_view`: the project's setting (its own choice, or the default for its model risk) and its effect.
BlindingView.title: BlindingView

BoundsProposalView.description: The bounds MS-01 §2.2 proposes for a parameter (`estimation.proposed_bounds`, D-34), or why none.
BoundsProposalView.title: BoundsProposalView

BriefCatalog.description: The brief's schema as the web form renders it (`modeler_project.brief.catalog`).
BriefCatalog.title: BriefCatalog

BriefImpact.description: A previewed brief edit: what it would change, nothing saved.
BriefImpact.title: BriefImpact

CPF.description: An immutable, versioned parameter document for one compound.
CPF.title: CPF

CampaignInputs.description: `campaign:prepare`: the staged CPF, MAP and observed PK a campaign starts from; a model system adds its own.
CampaignInputs.title: CampaignInputs

CampaignPackage.description:
The S7 package: the reproduction verdict, whether it may be exported (D13), hashes and the downloadable artifacts.
Server paths are never sent.
CampaignPackage.title: CampaignPackage

Chip.description: Where a value was read: a file, a part (p3, sheet:Name, body), a line and a cell of it.
Chip.title: Chip

ClientFileStarted.description:
A client file given at project start: read into Inputs at once (a filled template), triaged, or refused with the
reason.
ClientFileStarted.title: ClientFileStarted

ClientUpload.description: The files just stored (a filled template is read at once), and the page.
ClientUpload.title: ClientUpload

CoCompoundSpec.description:
Another compound of a model system in the simulation: dosed with its own protocol (an enantiomer, a co-dosed
parent) or, with no protocol, only formed (a metabolite).
CoCompoundSpec.title: CoCompoundSpec

CompanyPage.description:
One company: its people (each who has signed in) and its projects, archived ones included; its name, and why it is
disabled when it is.
CompanyPage.title: CompanyPage

CompetitiveInhibition.description: Reversible competitive inhibition of an enzyme/transporter (PK-Sim ``CompetitiveInhibition``).
CompetitiveInhibition.title: CompetitiveInhibition

CompoundRow.description:
One model input (`inputs_view.compound_rows`): kept, in conflict, held for a check, missing (S0 needs it), or
empty (a model input the data plan owns with no value yet: a row to fill, not counted as missing).
CompoundRow.title: CompoundRow

default: Cellular partition coefficient method - Rodgers and Rowland
calculation_methods.title: Calculation Methods

ContributionView.description: One thing the project took from a document (`library.Contribution`).
ContributionView.title: ContributionView

CoverageRow.description: One data-plan item and the evidence that covers it (`evidence_register.Coverage`).
CoverageRow.title: CoverageRow

CpfVersion.description: The assembled CPF's version, and the assembly report (what came from which evidence).
CpfVersion.title: CpfVersion

CpfView.description: `cpf_view.project_cpf_view`: the compound screen's parameter rows and the S0 completeness.
CpfView.title: CpfView

DataGrant.description: One cloud service a project's client files may be sent to: the client's written permission it rests on.
DataGrant.title: DataGrant

DataPermissionsView.description:
Where this project's client files may be sent for an AI model to read (the governance review, 2026-11-22):
in-house only unless a cloud service has the client's recorded permission. `services`: every cloud service there
is; `history`: each change, newest first.
DataPermissionsView.title: DataPermissionsView

DataPlanStatus.description: The data plan version a phase page is computed from, and its status.
DataPlanStatus.title: DataPlanStatus

DataRoomView.description: The Data room of one project, as the page and the report show it.
DataRoomView.title: DataRoomView

DatasetPoints.description: A dataset's points on its study's card (plan 2026-11-05 §3.2, `modeler_project.dataset_points`).
DatasetPoints.title: DatasetPoints

DefaultFit.description: The MS-01 §2.2 default the diagnosis may fit a candidate within, at its stages (D-37, `plan.default_fits`).
DefaultFit.title: DefaultFit

DeliveryArrival.description: One delivery (an arrival request) with its files.
DeliveryArrival.title: DeliveryArrival

DeliveryAssignment.description:
Values given their subject. A study is named by its id (`study`) or, when no file's label gave it one, by a
new label (`new_study`): one of them, and so a product (`product`, `new_product`), an arm of the study (`arm`,
`new_arm`), a batch of the product (`batch`, `new_batch`) and an analyte (`analyte`, `new_analyte`). Ids are the
ledger's (an analyte's: the page's `analytes`). An assignment replaces the earlier one whole: left out, it clears
the arm (the batch) the values had, and the values have the analyte the file gave, not one an earlier assignment
stated. A re-link that keeps a stated arm or analyte names it again.
DeliveryAssignment.title: DeliveryAssignment

DeliveryConfirmation.description: The subject's current confirmation with its signature manifestation and what its record says.
DeliveryConfirmation.title: DeliveryConfirmation

DeliveryConfirmationState.description: A subject's current confirmation as the page lists it (`intake_review.subjects`).
DeliveryConfirmationState.title: DeliveryConfirmationState

DeliveryCoverage.description: A file's coverage summary, from its coverage file (the current truth, `intake_records.CoverageSummary`).
DeliveryCoverage.title: DeliveryCoverage

DeliveryDecision.description:
A person's decision the subject's signature binds (plan 2026-11-14 §2.2.4), read from the intake's logs: who
made it, when and why, and what it is about. `scope` "subject": about the subject, or the clean-up of the files its
values were read from; "delivery": the clean-up of the delivery's other files, which the signature binds too
(contracts §11.10). For a blinded subject, or a decision about a file that holds a blinded study's values, the
digits of `why` are masked (as a region decision's are) and an entry gives no `value` (D-15).
DeliveryDecision.title: DeliveryDecision

DeliveryEntry.description:
A person's entry or correction of one value of the subject. `supersedes`: the value corrected (the new one
inherits its place in the series unless given). `arm`, `analyte`, `batch` are the ledger's entity ids.
DeliveryEntry.title: DeliveryEntry

DeliveryFileLink.description:
A person's link in force on this file's values (`link_carry.file_links`): what it covers here (`targets`: an
extract id for a whole table, else value ids; fact ids), how many values, where it sent them (entity ids, followed
through merges, with their labels), who linked them, when and why (the digits masked in a blinded file). Linking the
targets again replaces it whole.
DeliveryFileLink.title: DeliveryFileLink

DeliveryImpact.description:
What confirming the subject now would load, replace and set aside, and which artifacts it would make stale (a
signed MAP among them must be signed again), computed without signing or writing anything (the console redesign's
slice 4c). `supersedes`: the current confirmation the new one would supersede (null: a first confirmation).
DeliveryImpact.title: DeliveryImpact

DeliveryImpactChange.description: One dataset or evidence item of the landing as it would be decided (`intake_landing.LandingChange`).
DeliveryImpactChange.title: DeliveryImpactChange

DeliveryIndividual.description:
A study's simulated individual (D-29) as the landing would set it from the study's active values: one source
for the card, Populations and individuals, and what loads (`intake_landing.study_individual`).
DeliveryIndividual.title: DeliveryIndividual

DeliveryMappingApproval.description: `file_sha256` and `region_id` (both or neither): the table the answer shows the mapping on (as `GET` takes them).
DeliveryMappingApproval.title: DeliveryMappingApproval

DeliveryMappingEdit.description:
A person's version of the mapping: a `mapping/2` spec, checked on the table it was written for (the mapping's
sample table, or the table named).
DeliveryMappingEdit.title: DeliveryMappingEdit

DeliveryMappingField.description: A field of the ledger's vocabulary (`modeler_intake.fields`): what a value, a constant or a label is of.
DeliveryMappingField.title: DeliveryMappingField

DeliveryMappingProposal.description: A person's layout for a table named by its file and region: a `mapping/2` spec, checked by code on that table.
DeliveryMappingProposal.title: DeliveryMappingProposal

DeliveryMappingRejection.description: `file_sha256` and `region_id` (both or neither): the table the answer shows the mapping on (as `GET` takes them).
DeliveryMappingRejection.title: DeliveryMappingRejection

DeliveryMappingRow.description: A mapping version that waits for a person: proposed and in use, or rejected with its file not read again yet.
DeliveryMappingRow.title: DeliveryMappingRow

DeliveryMappingSample.description:
The table a mapping is shown on: its context lines, its header rows as the layout counts them (`header_rows`,
the layout's own: their cells as written, as each column's header is), and its first 5 and last 3 body rows with
every digit masked (`mapping.redact.redact_cell`): `body_rows` numbers them, so the rows left out are those of
`header_rows + 1 .. n_rows` not listed. For a file with a blinded study's values the body is withheld and the
digits of the header and the context lines are masked.
DeliveryMappingSample.title: DeliveryMappingSample

DeliveryMappingTable.description:
A table of the mapping's layout that one of its versions reads now (one row per table of `used_in`), and how the
version shown reads it: `reads` false when that version has an error on the table (`findings`: its errors and
notes there, their digits masked for a file that holds a blinded study's values), null when the table's source
model is not cached. `newer`: the table stays with an older version because the newest approved one does not read
it (as on the page's region). `moves`: the version shown waits for approval, and approving it moves the table to
it (final review round 3: said before the approval, never found after it); null otherwise.
DeliveryMappingTable.title: DeliveryMappingTable

DeliveryMappingVocabulary.description:
The words a mapping spec (`mapping/2`) is written with, read from `modeler_intake.mapping_spec` and
`modeler_intake.fields`: a form that edits a layout offers these and never makes one up.
DeliveryMappingVocabulary.title: DeliveryMappingVocabulary

DeliveryNewerLayout.description:
The newest approved version of a table's layout, newer than the version the table is read with, that does not
read it: the pipeline reads a table only with an approved version that has no error on the table's own grid
(`intake_pipeline._choose`), so the table stays with the older one. `findings`: that version's errors on this table
(their digits masked for a file that holds a blinded study's values); `constants`: that version's facts read once
for the table, which a finding's location names by number.
DeliveryNewerLayout.title: DeliveryNewerLayout

DeliveryOutside.description:
An item with a number outside every region that is not page furniture. `counted`: it is in the summary's
`outside_numeric` (no mapped table cites it and no person accepted it as not data), so it blocks a confirmation.
Not counted with no `decision`: a table that is read cites it (a fact read once for the table).
DeliveryOutside.title: DeliveryOutside

DeliveryRegion.description:
One region of a file and what was done with it. `state` is `waiting` while the file is being read again, or its
mapping was rejected and the run that follows has not finished (its earlier values are still in the ledger).
DeliveryRegion.title: DeliveryRegion

DeliveryRegionDecision.description:
A person's "not data" decision in force on a region or an outside item (a `RegionDecision`, rd-n): who made it,
when and why. For a file that holds a blinded study's values, the digits of `why` are masked (a person may have
quoted what the file holds).
DeliveryRegionDecision.title: DeliveryRegionDecision

DeliveryRegionHead.description:
The first rows of a table no layout reads (never read, or its layout rejected), for a person to give it a
layout: at most 5 rows and 30 columns, each cell as written (cut at 80 characters, "" for an empty one). For a file
that holds a blinded study's values, only the header band (its rows above the first row of values, as a mapping's
sample shows it) with every digit masked: no row of values. `spans` gives, for each of `rows`, each column's width
as the file draws it: 1; n > 1 for a merged cell's first column, over n columns; 0 for a column a merged cell to its
left covers (its text in `rows` is the merged cell's, copied as a mapping reads a merged header).
DeliveryRegionHead.title: DeliveryRegionHead

DeliveryRegionRestore.description:
The latest "Restore…" that gave a region or an outside item back (a `RegionDecision` with `restores`): who, when,
why (masked as a decision's is) and the decisions it undid. It stays the item's record when a later decision sets
the item aside again.
DeliveryRegionRestore.title: DeliveryRegionRestore

DeliveryRelink.description:
A person's link a re-read of its table did not carry over (`link_carry.waiting`): the values of `targets` (extract
or fact ids on the "study not stated" list now) were read from the table that `assignment` linked, in part (`whole`
false: which part it would cover now cannot be told), or whole before links were carried over. Where it sent them
(entity ids, followed through merges), who linked them, when and why (the digits masked when the study is blinded).
DeliveryRelink.title: DeliveryRelink

DeliveryRestore.description: Regions (or outside items) a person marked as not data, given back: the same ids and scope as the exclusion.
DeliveryRestore.title: DeliveryRestore

DeliveryRules.description: The intake rules file a record was computed with (SME-governed: UNVERIFIED until signed).
DeliveryRules.title: DeliveryRules

DeliverySource.description:
A `SourceView` (§4.2) plus the file and the value. `blinded`: the region holds a value of a blinded study, so
its cells with a number and the cells a value is anchored at are blank, every digit of the text and the title is
masked, and the page is not given (it must not be drawn).
DeliverySource.title: DeliverySource

DeliverySpotValue.description:
One value of the draw with the tuple it is ticked for (`value`) and its source reference (`value.id` for
`/delivery/source?value=`, `value.anchor`, `value.locators`).
DeliverySpotValue.title: DeliverySpotValue

DeliveryTable.description: The subject's values of one table (an extract), or its scalar facts of one file (`kind` facts).
DeliveryTable.title: DeliveryTable

DeliveryTableMove.description:
What approving the version shown (one waiting for approval) changes for a table of its layout: the pipeline's
own rule (`intake_pipeline.choose_version`: of the approved versions that read a table, the one leaving the fewest
numbers unread, then reading the most facts once, then the newest) would read it with that version instead of the
one it is read with now (`from_version`). What changes: the numbers its reading leaves unread, before and after,
and the facts read once for the whole table (by field) that it no longer reads or newly reads.
DeliveryTableMove.title: DeliveryTableMove

DeliveryUnreadCell.description:
A cell with a number in a read table that no part of its layout reads (silent: it holds up the delivery's
signatures), and why, as code's reading of the table records it (`CellUse.rule`): "" (no column or row rule of the
layout reads it), "unparseable" (a column reads it, but it is not a plain number), "time_unparseable" (its time is
not a plain number), "qualifier_twice" (a second spread, n or interval for one value), "lloq_differs" (its LLOQ is
not the table's), "time_unit_conflict" (the cell writes another time unit than its column). `text` is null for a
file that holds a blinded study's values. Read-only: a single cell is not set aside here (plan 2026-11-14 §3 API 3,
the owner's review).
DeliveryUnreadCell.title: DeliveryUnreadCell

DeliveryValue.description:
One value of the ledger (a fact, or the i-th value of a table's extract) with the tuple it is read with: value,
unit, time, labels and statistic. `blinded`: what D-15 withholds is null.
DeliveryValue.title: DeliveryValue

Deviation.description:
A change to the plan after its MAP was signed (D-14, ICH M15 §4.2): it applies to campaigns only once the MIDD
lead signs it, which makes a new MAP version superseding the signed one.
Deviation.title: Deviation

DiffRow.description: A departure from the MS-01 default (`modeler_project.plan.diff`); `proposal` only on a pending A5 proposal.
DiffRow.title: DiffRow

Disposition.description: D1: binding and distribution, then each elimination / transport pathway.
Disposition.title: Disposition

DocumentsAdded.description: The documents added, and which of them are read for data (plan 2026-11-10, R2).
DocumentsAdded.title: DocumentsAdded

DocumentsRead.description: The library's documents now read for data (queued for the reading agent), and the ones not read, with why.
DocumentsRead.title: DocumentsRead

DosePhaseSpec.description: One phase of a regimen: ``repetitions`` doses of ``dose``, ``interval_h`` apart, the first at ``start_h``.
DosePhaseSpec.title: DosePhaseSpec

EngineBinding.description:
Where a parameter lives in a PK-Sim snapshot (MS-01 §2.1).

`building_block` is Compound/Individual/Formulation/Protocol. For a compound process the `process`
field carries the process internal name and, for molecule-based processes, the molecule after a
colon, e.g. "MetabolizationSpecific_FirstOrder:CYP3A4"; `parameter` is the engine parameter name.
Individual, Simulation and ExpressionProfile bindings carry the full PK-Sim path in `parameter`. A Simulation
binding's `route` limits it to the simulations dosed that way (the published model sets it only there).
EngineBinding.title: EngineBinding

EngineIdentity.description: What produced the numbers: real PK-Sim, a software fixture, or an injected engine (never read as PBPK).
EngineIdentity.title: EngineIdentity

EngineStatus.description:
Whether the engine answers (R-N08, `engine_check`): its kind, the command's words, the engine id and image
digest it records (null while the digest is the development placeholder), and what was checked, in words.
EngineStatus.title: EngineStatus

EscalationItem.description: An open escalation as one person reads it: the stored record, and whether this person may decide it.
EscalationItem.title: EscalationItem

EscalationResolved.description: A signed decision applied to a single-node campaign: the stage's new status (and the stages still to run).
EscalationResolved.title: EscalationResolved

EstimationRow.description: One numeric parameter of the estimation plan (`review.estimation_rows`): fixed (no fit) or estimated.
EstimationRow.title: EstimationRow

EvidenceChoice.description: A value kept for its parameter: the ids of the other values it rejected, and the page.
EvidenceChoice.title: EvidenceChoice

EvidenceCorrection.description: A corrected copy of a value, and the page.
EvidenceCorrection.title: EvidenceCorrection

EvidenceView.description: An evidence item as the page shows it (`inputs.evidence_view`): the value in both units, its source and grade.
EvidenceView.title: EvidenceView

ExpressionSpec.description:
An enzyme, transporter or other-protein expression profile. Real OSP transporter profiles carry no
Localization (PK-Sim supplies it for the named transporter), so it is emitted only when set; enzymes keep
the standard intracellular localization by default.

``harvested`` is a profile copied verbatim from an OSP reference snapshot (`pbpk_domain.expression`): its
per-organ relative expressions, half-lives, transport directions and ontogeny. Without those every organ's
relative expression is zero and the protein's processes do nothing, so a campaign build always uses a
harvested profile; the bare form (molecule and reference concentration only) exists for builder tests.
ExpressionSpec.title: ExpressionSpec

field.description: a dotted field from the vocabulary, or a new dotted name
field.title: Field

product.description: the product (as named on the question card) the fact concerns, if any
product.title: Product

quote.description: the verbatim text from the file that contains the value (one to three lines)
quote.title: Quote

subject.description: what the fact is about, as written (a study, product, batch, code, subject)
subject.title: Subject

value.description: the value exactly as written in the file
value.title: Value

FeedbackEvidence.description: New evidence after an S5 failure (plan §12.3 N4 c): one parameter's measured value, in the CPF's own unit.
FeedbackEvidence.title: FeedbackEvidence

FigureSuggestion.description: A figure worth digitizing: no table holds its values (plan 2026-11-10, R5).
FigureSuggestion.title: FigureSuggestion

FigureView.description: An image placed on a PDF page (`modeler_intake.documents.PdfFigure`): its box as fractions of the page as shown.
FigureView.title: FigureView

FileTagView.description: What a client file is, as the person said at upload (`documents.FileTag`): a hint for reading it, not a fact.
FileTagView.title: FileTagView

reason.description: one plain sentence: what the file is and why it is (not) needed
reason.title: Reason

FitGroup.description:
Parameters fitted as one (PI-4 B, docs/plans/2026-11-02-pi-4b-relative-group.md): each member is simulated at
f x its current value, so the split between them is kept and the data estimate only the factor f ("Use as Factor"
in the OSP desktop). A person chooses a group and signs it with the MAP: why the members are fitted as one
(``reason``) and where their split comes from (``split_source``, e.g. the in vitro fractions metabolised). The
factor's bounds contain 1, the members' current values.
FitGroup.title: FitGroup

FitGroupChoice.description:
Estimated parameters a person fits as one, through one factor (PI-4 B2): each at f x its start value, so their
split is kept. Why (``reason``) and where the split comes from (``split_source``, e.g. the in vitro fractions
metabolised and their reference) are required; both are signed with the MAP.
FitGroupChoice.title: FitGroupChoice

FitGroupRow.description: Estimated parameters a person fits as one, through one factor (PI-4 B2, `review.fit_group_rows`).
FitGroupRow.title: FitGroupRow

FormulationWayView.description:
What gives a tablet study its formulation as the project stands (`modeler_project.formulation_way`): use a
product's dissolution profile as its release (`products`: those whose profile can), add a product's dissolution data
(`products`: those here, or the one the study names), add a product (none is here), or choose the formulation a study
used (several are in the model). `studies`: the tablet studies it is for; `ready`: the first product's profile can be
used now (its product's dissolution data confirmed), else they are confirmed first; `each`: every study's own lever
(round 5: a study that names its product is settled by that product only).
FormulationWayView.title: FormulationWayView

GiveProjects.description:
`to`: who receives them (someone who has signed in to the company); `from_`: whose projects they are, or empty
for every project of the company (those made before memberships were kept, or outside the web, included).
GiveProjects.title: GiveProjects

HarvestedProcess.description:
A process of a type in HARVESTED_PROCESSES, written with exactly the parameters the CPF carries for it (PK-Sim
computes the ones a snapshot leaves out, e.g. kcat from an in-vitro Vmax).
HarvestedProcess.title: HarvestedProcess

Health.description: The API is up, which deployment it is, and how it verifies a sign-in ("dev": the DEV verifier, never Part 11).
Health.title: Health

HeldFixed.description: An MS-01 candidate a person keeps fixed (D-37).
HeldFixed.title: HeldFixed

HistoryRow.description: One version of an artifact, and the field changes from the previous one (blinded values left out).
HistoryRow.title: HistoryRow

Hold.description: An MS-01 fit candidate a person keeps fixed: the diagnosis does not fit it within MS-01's default (D-37).
Hold.title: Hold

IdentityProposal.description: The structure proposed as evidence (its id), and the page.
IdentityProposal.title: IdentityProposal

ImpactView.description: `deps.impact_view`: what a change would replace and which downstream artifacts it makes stale.
ImpactView.title: ImpactView

InputRow.description: One PK-Sim input: the building block, the PK-Sim (or CPF) name, the value, its source and status.
InputRow.title: InputRow

InputStudyRow.description: One study (`inputs_view.study_rows`): its facts without observed values, proposed role, blinding, demographics.
InputStudyRow.title: InputStudyRow

IntravenousBolusProtocolSpec.description:
An IV bolus: PK-Sim ``IntravenousBolus`` with a start time and InputDose, no infusion time (harvested from the
OSP Alfentanil, Midazolam, Digoxin, Metformin and Verapamil protocols, simple and schema form).
IntravenousBolusProtocolSpec.title: IntravenousBolusProtocolSpec

KeyAdd.description:
A key to store. Every field is optional to the validator and checked by the handler, so a refusal never echoes the
request (FastAPI's 422 answer repeats the input it rejects, which here holds a secret).
KeyAdd.title: KeyAdd

KeyView.description:
A stored key, never its secret: the secret fields' last 4 characters and the plain fields (an address, a
region). `due`: active for `rotate_after_days` or longer.
KeyView.title: KeyView

LibraryEntryView.description: A document's entry in the library after a change: what it relates to, and its withdrawal if withdrawn.
LibraryEntryView.title: LibraryEntryView

LibraryRowView.description: One document of the project library (`library.LibraryRow`), with what it contributed.
LibraryRowView.title: LibraryRowView

LimitRow.description:
One monthly limit and this month's use against it (spend at the page's prices, tokens in and out). `level`:
`ok` below `warn_at` of every measure, `warn` from there, `over` once a measure is reached. A limit only warns.
LimitRow.title: LimitRow

LimitSet.description:
A limit on a company (`subject` empty), a project (its id) or a person (their subject), each month: the estimated
spend in USD and the tokens in and out. A measure left empty has no limit; both empty removes the limit.
LimitSet.title: LimitSet

LimitTarget.description: A company, with the projects and people a limit can be set on.
LimitTarget.title: LimitTarget

LimitsPage.description:
The monthly limits (console, E): each with this month's use; those at 80 % or past; the changes; what a limit can
be set on. A limit warns the administrator and never stops an agent; the companies' people never see it.
LimitsPage.title: LimitsPage

LiteratureRun.description:
Where the literature agent stands (plan 2026-11-05 §3.3): searching or not, its latest run (the structured
sources' reading is one, `A2-sources`), the turns it has taken of its budget, the values it has proposed so far (they
flow into the inputs when it finishes), and what the structured sources gave.
LiteratureRun.title: LiteratureRun

MadeBy.description:
Who wrote one stage's answer for one file (or, `file` empty, for the delivery): the evidence report's "How this
report was made" (the governance review, 2026-11-22). `service`: where the model ran ("our server", or the cloud
service the file was sent to); `switches`: each model that could not answer before it, and why.
MadeBy.title: MadeBy

MapApplication.description:
An application the question of interest pins (T-31): its analysis template, pinned by version, and the
person's inputs to it. An input the template marks ``never_default`` is the person's to give; until it is
given the application names it (`problems`) and the MAP cannot be signed.
MapApplication.title: MapApplication

MapReading.description:
A confirmed reading: the preview's fields, the datasets it proposed and the page, merged into one object
(today's shape; the owner chose to keep it, 2026-10-08). Where both name a key the page's wins: `dissolution` is
the page's profiles and comparisons, not the preview's record count.
MapReading.title: MapReading

MapRiskAssessment.description:
The ICH M15 model risk assessment (§2.1.5) as Start recorded it, under the MAP's hash (the owner's item 5 of
2026-11-02): each rating and why it is what it is (a person's words, or an agent's draft a person confirmed), why the
tier when the two ratings differ, and each rating a person kept against the intake agent's suggestion, with the
person's reason.
MapRiskAssessment.title: MapRiskAssessment

MapVersion.description: The latest MAP version, its hash and the campaign inputs its signature staged.
MapVersion.title: MapVersion

MappingBody.description:
How to read a sheet: the page's form (`form`) or a mapping recipe (`proposal`, the data-mapping agent's shape or
written by a person); the study facts the sheet does not state; and whether to keep the result (False: preview).
MappingBody.title: MappingBody

MeView.description: The signed-in person: what the web app shows them (the console's link only to the platform's owner).
MeView.title: MeView

Measured.description: A value with its unit and provenance, as it will appear in the snapshot.
Measured.title: Measured

MembersPage.description:
The project's members, and the people who signed in to this workspace and are not members yet. `managed` is
false where the principal's access comes from the deployment rather than memberships (the DEV sign-in's `*`).
MembersPage.title: MembersPage

MichaelisMentenMetabolism.description:
Saturable enzyme metabolism (PK-Sim ``MetabolizationSpecific_MM``). Parameter names and units are
from the OSP Rifampicin model; Vmax and Km are the identifiable pair (MS-01 §2.2), kcat and enzyme
concentration are optional and only emitted when supplied.
MichaelisMentenMetabolism.title: MichaelisMentenMetabolism

MicrosomalMichaelisMenten.description:
Saturable metabolism scaled from liver microsomes (PK-Sim ``MetabolizationLiverMicrosomes_MM``). Names and
units are from the OSP Midazolam model (CYP3A4, UGT1A4): the in-vitro Vmax per mg microsomal protein and, where
the model sets it, the enzyme content of the microsomes; Km; and kcat, which the published model fits and which
then governs the in-vivo rate.
MicrosomalMichaelisMenten.title: MicrosomalMichaelisMenten

ModelChoice.description:
A one-click choice on an agent's row (plan 2026-11-21 v2 §9): Qwen Coder, Claude or gpt-oss-120b. `tools`: it
calls tools; `reads_scans`: it reads a page image itself (Claude only); `has_active_key`: its provider has one.
ModelChoice.title: ModelChoice

OverallStudy.description: A study of Overall Data: what the plan knows about it, and where it is placed now.
OverallStudy.title: OverallStudy

Overview.description:
Every company (tenant) with its people, projects and agent use; the platform's state; the limits this month's use
has reached 80 % of, or passed (`warnings`, for the administrator only).
Overview.title: Overview

ParamNode.description: A CPF parameter on D1 / D2, with its fit choice and the stages that may fit it; D2 nodes carry no source.
ParamNode.title: ParamNode

ParticleFormulationSpec.description:
Particle dissolution (PK-Sim ``Formulation_Particles``, Noyes-Whitney) with a monodisperse size distribution,
as the OSP Ketoconazole model writes it: the unstirred water layer thickness, the distribution type (0:
monodisperse, the only one placed here) and the mean particle radius. Dissolution is limited by the compound's
solubility, so a "solution" given as 8 nm particles (the model's PD_solution) still respects it.
ParticleFormulationSpec.title: ParticleFormulationSpec

PeoplePage.description:
The console's people (F). `ready` false: Keycloak is not set up for the console, `problem` says what to do.
`smtp`: Keycloak can email a person their set-password link; without it the owner sets a first password in
Keycloak's own console (`notice_link`). Passwords never pass through the platform.
PeoplePage.title: PeoplePage

PersonChange.description: What changes: whether they can sign in, roles given or taken, their company. Omitted: unchanged.
PersonChange.title: PersonChange

PersonReset.description:
A lost authenticator (removed; set up again at the next sign-in) and/or a forgotten password (Keycloak's email
link, or a temporary one set by the owner in Keycloak's console: the platform never handles it).
PersonReset.title: PersonReset

PipelineCounts.description:
What the intake pipeline's own run lines add up to (`modeler_project.intake_health`): counts only, no file
name, no value, no project name.
PipelineCounts.title: PipelineCounts

PipelineHealth.description: Where the intake pipeline is blind, per company and in all (contracts 2026-11-12 §8.10; plan §7.8).
PipelineHealth.title: PipelineHealth

PipelineStage.description: A stage's times over the files' latest runs: how many timings, their median and their 90th percentile (seconds).
PipelineStage.title: PipelineStage

PlacementPreview.description: A move's dry run: what the validator and the diff would say; nothing is saved.
PlacementPreview.title: PlacementPreview

PlanSigned.description: The page after `plan:sign`, and the signature the MAP carries.
PlanSigned.title: PlanSigned

objective.default: Predict exposure for the question of interest
objective.title: Objective

role.description: the product's part in the comparison: reference, test, original, reformulated or other
role.title: Role

ProjectSystem.description:
`GET /projects/{id}/system`: the project's model system, or none for a single compound. `links` is the stored
document a client edits and puts back (`PUT /projects/{id}/system`).
ProjectSystem.title: ProjectSystem

Proposal.description: An A5 departure from the plan, shown in the diff until a person accepts or rejects it.
Proposal.title: Proposal

PublishedModel.description: A published OSP model of the project's drug, which the Inputs step can take as a source.
PublishedModel.title: PublishedModel

PublishedModelTaken.description:
What taking a published OSP model as a source proposed: its values and datasets, those it had already given,
and what it left out, with why.
PublishedModelTaken.title: PublishedModelTaken

quotes.description: the facts the card rests on, each quoted
quotes.title: Quotes

QuestionRecord.description: A question of interest the project answers.
QuestionRecord.title: QuestionRecord

RatingDisagreementView.description: A person's M15 rating that differs from the intake agent's suggestion (`brief.rating_disagreements`).
RatingDisagreementView.title: RatingDisagreementView

ReadingItem.description: One file in the project's reading queue (plan 2026-11-10, R3: the reading tray).
ReadingItem.title: ReadingItem

ReadingQueuePage.description: The reading tray: each file the reading agent is to read, is reading or has read, and whether agents are on.
ReadingQueuePage.title: ReadingQueuePage

RealDataSummary.description: What a round's verdict rests on (`pbpk_domain.data_origin.real_data_summary`, plan §9.4).
RealDataSummary.title: RealDataSummary

ReconciledRow.description: One client item of the data plan and what arrived for it (`client_data.Reconciled`).
ReconciledRow.title: ReconciledRow

RelatesToView.description: What a document relates to (`documents.RelatesTo`): a step and, optionally, a task within it.
RelatesToView.title: RelatesToView

ReleaseProposal.description: A profile's fit proposed as release-model evidence: the evidence ids, and the page.
ReleaseProposal.title: ReleaseProposal

RequestLineView.description: One thing the project asks the client to send (`requirements.client_request`, page review 1 decision 2b).
RequestLineView.title: RequestLineView

RetrievalView.description: Where an agent took a document from, and what of it is held (`documents.Retrieval`; open-access full text only).
RetrievalView.title: RetrievalView

ReviewFinish.description: What a sheet read by code needs, given on its card (build C2): the study's or product's facts.
ReviewFinish.title: ReviewFinish

ReviewGroup.description: A study, a product or a file's compound values, to confirm or confirmed.
ReviewGroup.title: ReviewGroup

ReviewIssue.description: A conflict, an explainable difference or a question on a group: open until a person confirms a selection.
ReviewIssue.title: ReviewIssue

ReviewRisk.description: The ICH M15 model risk the MAP will carry, and what Start says of it.
ReviewRisk.title: ReviewRisk

ReviewRow.description: One model input as the review table shows it (`modeler_project.review.review_rows`).
ReviewRow.title: ReviewRow

ReviewSource.description: Where the kept value comes from (the evidence item's source, with its type).
ReviewSource.title: ReviewSource

chosen.description: the id of one of the decision's options
chosen.title: Chosen

RoomDecision.description: A modeling choice waiting for the modeler (named apart from the API's other decisions).
RoomDecision.title: RoomDecision

key.description: the input it fills (a PK-Sim input's name)
key.title: Key

reason.description: why this value: entered by a person, it needs one
reason.title: Reason

RoomPublication.description:
What "Send to the model" would send now (`modeler_project.dataroom.publish.plan_publication`, nothing written),
and what keeps it from being sent, in words.
RoomPublication.title: RoomPublication

reason.description: why the inputs are sent now (kept with the signature)
reason.title: Reason

RoomPublished.description: What was sent, signed: items written, items already in the project (skipped), and the signature.
RoomPublished.title: RoomPublished

RoomRun.description: The Data room's background run (`modeler_agents.dataroom.run_room`): each stage with its live counts and note.
RoomRun.title: RoomRun

files.description: the per-file stages for these files only (their paths)
files.title: Files

redo.description: stages whose kept answers are made again
redo.title: Redo

stages.description: the stages to run (none named: every stage)
stages.title: Stages

RoomStudy.description: One clinical study as the room shows it (named apart from the API's other study views).
RoomStudy.title: RoomStudy

RoomUpload.description: One upload as stored: a file or an archive, its bytes in the project's blobs.
RoomUpload.title: RoomUpload

RoomUploaded.description: What an upload added: `added` the uploads of this request (a file sent twice is stored once), `uploads` all.
RoomUploaded.title: RoomUploaded

RunSummary.description:
One agent run as a page lists it: the run record's own keys (`run_store.start_run` writes all of them; the run
is unfinished while `finished_at` is null). Not every page lists the provider.
RunSummary.title: RunSummary

Sample.description: What the recipe read, in a person's terms (values withheld for an external study before the MAP is signed).
Sample.title: Sample

SeriesPoints.description: One series of a dataset, as the card draws and tabulates it, with code's statistics of a profile.
SeriesPoints.title: SeriesPoints

SheetForm.description: What a person tells the page about one sheet. Columns are letters; rows are the sheet's own row numbers.

header_row.description: The row with the column headers (times across: the times)
header_row.title: Header Row

SheetForm.title: SheetForm

SheetView.description: One sheet as text, the reading form's first filling and what was found.
SheetView.title: SheetView

SignatureCreated.description: A Part 11 signature, from the token's step-up (never a password).
SignatureCreated.title: SignatureCreated

SignatureRegister.description: A project's signatures, newest first, and whether the company's audit chain verifies (a broken chain says so).
SignatureRegister.title: SignatureRegister

SignatureRow.description: One signature given on a record of a project (R-N09), read from the company's audit chain (`signature.create`).
SignatureRow.title: SignatureRow

SnapshotPreview.description: A built and validated PK-Sim snapshot, not persisted; the snapshot is PK-Sim's own JSON.
SnapshotPreview.title: SnapshotPreview

SourceFile.description: A delivered file as the source viewer opens it: its pages (with their size) or its parts of lines.
SourceFile.title: SourceFile

SourcePart.description: One part of a file (a sheet, a Word or text body, a page's lines), numbered as the agents read it.
SourcePart.title: SourcePart

SpecificBinding.description: Specific binding to a target (PK-Sim ``SpecificBinding``); names/units from the OSP Midazolam model.
SpecificBinding.title: SpecificBinding

StaleArtifacts.description: What was made from inputs that have since changed, with why (shown on the History page).
StaleArtifacts.title: StaleArtifacts

StartBlock.description: What Start still needs (`steps.start_issues`), and the parts the screen draws from.
StartBlock.title: StartBlock

StartIssueView.description: One thing Start still needs, on the brief field it belongs to (`steps.start_issues`).
StartIssueView.title: StartIssueView

StepRow.description:
One step of the redesigned flow (Start, Inputs, Review & sign, Run) and what it waits on; Inputs, while a tablet
study has no formulation, with the lever that gives it one (the step bar and Review & sign name it: round 4).
StepRow.title: StepRow

objective.default: Predict exposure for the question of interest
objective.title: Objective

StudyRow.description: An observed study as stored for the project. D-15: a blinded external study comes without its profile.
StudyRow.title: StudyRow

StudyView.description: What the plan knows about a study (from the P4 catalog): enough to plan and validate, no observed values.
StudyView.title: StudyView

StudyWayView.description:
One tablet study's own lever (`modeler_project.formulation_way.StudyWay`): `products` in the order a link opens
them, `ready` whether the first one's profile can be used now, `named` the product the study names, if any; `uses`
(round 7, To do's item only) the formulation the model would use for it while that is another product's.
StudyWayView.title: StudyWayView

SystemAnalyte.description: What a study can measure, and where MS-01 v1.3 judges it (§6.5).
SystemAnalyte.title: SystemAnalyte

SystemFormation.description: A process of `compound` that forms `metabolite` (the published model's `Metabolite` link).
SystemFormation.title: SystemFormation

SystemStatus.description: System status's own read (R-N08): the deployment, the execution backend and the engine.
SystemStatus.title: SystemStatus

SystemView.description: The project's model system as stored (`pbpk_domain.system`): compounds, roles, products, analytes.
SystemView.title: SystemView

TagProposalView.description: Another tag code read from the file's content, with what prompted it (`documents.TagProposal`).
TagProposalView.title: TagProposalView

TemplateContent.description:
A starting point in full. The CPF and the studies are the template's own documents, in the upload shapes they
are sent back in (a reference model's CPF, the blank one's empty parameters; studies with their origin).
TemplateContent.title: TemplateContent

TransporterMichaelisMenten.description:
Saturable active transport (PK-Sim ``ActiveTransportSpecific_MM``). Names/units from the OSP
Rifampicin model. The transporter needs an expression profile (``ExpressionSpec`` type Transporter).
TransporterMichaelisMenten.title: TransporterMichaelisMenten

Uncertainty.description: A fitted parameter's precision, from the parameter identification's confidence-interval estimate.
Uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

UnreadableRecord.description:
A stored record this build cannot read (a key it needs is missing, a value of the wrong kind), named with why,
so one record written in an earlier shape no longer fails its whole list (`modeler_api.stored_records`).
UnreadableRecord.title: UnreadableRecord

Usage.description:
Agent runs and their tokens; `usd`: what they would cost on the Claude model the page is priced at, with their
conversations cached (an estimate: the tokens are the model's that ran them).
Usage.title: Usage

UsagePage.description:
Agent use since a date, per agent, project, person, company and day, and the runs themselves (newest first, at
most `limit`). `prices`: USD per million tokens of `priced_as` (input, cache write, cache read, output).
UsagePage.title: UsagePage

ValidationStage.description: What S4 or S5 judges under the MAP this plan generates, and what happens when it fails (MS-01 §4, §6.6).
ValidationStage.title: ValidationStage

Value.description: One input or finding, as the report shows it: value, unit, source(s), status.
Value.title: Value

ValueReuseOffer.description:
Another project of the same drug the person can open, and the literature and public-source values it holds that
this one does not (plan 2026-11-05 §3.3; a client's data never leaves its project).
ValueReuseOffer.title: ValueReuseOffer

VersionView.description: `deps.version_view`: an artifact version's identity, status, provenance and approvals (content when asked).
VersionView.title: VersionView

WithdrawalView.description: Who withdrew a document, when and why (`documents.Withdrawal`).
WithdrawalView.title: WithdrawalView

modeler_api__views__admin__PersonView.description:
A person of the realm as Keycloak keeps them: their company (`tenant_id`), roles, whether they can sign in and
have set up their authenticator, and what Keycloak will ask of them at their next sign-in.
modeler_api__views__admin__PersonView.title: PersonView

put.description:
What every agent goes on with when its own model fails, in order (the owner, 2026-11-22: "switch at that moment to
another, so the task continues"). Signed with the step-up and audited: a cloud model here receives client files.

Put every agent on one provider and model in one step (the owner, 2026-11-11: "I must be able to switch between
any of them easily", for when Claude on Bedrock is lost and the in-house model takes over, or back). Each agent's
change is its own audit event with the same reason. Refused, with nothing changed, when the provider has no active
key: a switch made in a hurry must not leave every agent with nothing to run on.

post.description: A new company (a tenant): its folder in the store, its name, and its own audit chain from its first event.

Every person of the company can no longer sign in (their sessions end as their tokens expire); its projects,
records and people are kept, and enabling it lets the same people in again.

Make a person a member of another person's projects, or of all the company's, and with `owner` their owner: how
the projects made under the pilot's DEV sign-in (its "dev-user") reach the people who sign in through Keycloak. Each
membership and change of owner is an audit event on the company's chain, by the administrator, with the reason.

put.description: Set, change or remove a monthly limit (a fresh step-up and a reason; an audit event on the owner's chain).

post.description: A new person of a company, in Keycloak: they set their own password and authenticator at their first sign-in.

get.description:
Where the intake pipeline is blind, per company and in all (contracts 2026-11-12 §8.10): the files by state, the
share of tables mapped from the cache, by a rule, by the LLM and left unread, parser failures, unsupported files by
extension, outside items, unresolved anchors, pages needing OCR, and each stage's median and 90th-percentile time.
Counts from the pipeline's own run lines only: no file name, no value. `since`: the runs queued from that day.

System status (P-32, R-N08): the deployment, the execution backend, and whether the engine answers, its
configured command started without a job (`engine_check`; kept a minute; nothing is simulated).
List the tenant's campaigns (summary + stage/round detail); ``?project=`` narrows to one project.

One campaign's monitor view. 404 when it is not in the tenant; 403 when the caller is not a member of
the campaign's project (checked after the lookup, since the project is a property of the campaign, not the URL).

post.description: Record a signed deviation from the MAP and inform the running stage workflow.

get.description:
The S7 package: reproduction verdict, whether it may be exported (D13), hashes, and the downloadable
artifacts. Server paths are never returned.

Download the package zip or the rendered MAR. The zip is refused while reproduction has not passed (D13);
only files inside the object store are ever served.

post.description: Resume an escalated stage with a signed decision. The signature is verified before any signal is sent.
Resume, accept or abort an escalated stage of a single-node campaign, with a Part 11 signature.

get.description: The client-data workbook (D-11): README plus one sheet per kind of data, read with no AI.

Open campaign escalations awaiting a signed decision, of the projects this person is a member of. An escalation
names its campaign, not its project, so its project is its campaign's; one whose campaign is not (yet) recorded has
no project to check and stays listed, as a campaign with no project does (the decision pop-up reads this list alone,
so a decision is asked even before its campaign's record can be read).

post.description: Check an ICH M15 assessment table for completeness and the model risk its ratings allow (a curator or reviewer).
Build and validate a snapshot without persisting it (a curator or reviewer: redesign review R-S04).

parameters.description: Comma list of extra parts: steps, owner
parameters.name: with

schema.description: Comma list of extra parts: steps, owner
schema.title: With

post.description: A person supplies the paper the agent asked for; it is stored as a citable document.

get.description:
The project's agent runs, newest first, `limit` at a time; `before` (a run's id, the last page's `next_before`)
gives the older ones after it (R-N05). Only this company's runs of this project.

This project's audit events (newest first) and whether the tenant's chain verifies: its artifacts' events, and the
events on the project itself (its members, archiving and restoring).

put.description: The MIDD lead's choice for this project (D-15), with its reason, on the audit chain.

Change fields (no reason asked, D-27). A model risk outside what its ICH M15 ratings admit is refused. With
``preview`` the impact is returned and nothing is saved; otherwise the data plan follows the new brief.

post.description:
Start a modeling campaign through the configured execution backend (local single-node, or Temporal). Outside
development, only on a MAP a person signed and on the CPF it signed (`modeler_api.run_guard`).

get.description:
The project's data request (page review 1, decision 2b): the client-data workbook with a first sheet listing what
only the client can send, from the data plan, and where each goes. The client fills it and sends it back.

One sheet as text, with the reading form to check: the reading agent's checked proposal when there is one, else
code's first filling (units, dose and LLOQ quoted from their cells; what the sheet does not say left for the
person), and the notes that say what was found and what was not.

post.description: A person says what a sheet holds (overrides code and A4).

Apply a mapping recipe deterministically. Preview shows the records, problems and open questions; confirming a
recipe with none of them creates the datasets (origin CLIENT) and keeps the recipe on the file's record.

A4 proposes how to read the file's data sheets, in the background; each proposal is checked by code and waits on
its sheet for the person to check and save (nothing is read into the project until then). A client PDF or Word file
is read for its study facts, profiles, NCA tables, dissolution and study-name links instead (I4); what code accepts
waits on Inputs, in its study or product, until a person confirms it.

get.description:
What the client's files gave, grouped where it belongs (a study, a product, the compound values of a file), each
group to confirm or confirmed, with its conflicts and questions settled or open.

post.description:
Confirm a group: its selections are applied and its datasets and values load into the project, in one audited
record. Refused while a conflict or question of the group is open.
An item-level edit before the group is confirmed: one fact of a study (the audit keeps before and after).

Give what a sheet read by code needs (plan 2026-11-05 §3.1, build C2): once nothing is left, the reading is saved
like the sheet reader's (its datasets wait on the card to confirm); else the answers are kept and the rest asked.
Change a settled conflict or question before its group is confirmed.

Confirm the selection on a conflict or a question (an option, or the value a question asks for); no reason is
asked. It stays changeable until the group is confirmed.

get.description:
The compound's CPF: the one Inputs assembles for the project (the system of record every simulation of a pipeline
project is regenerated from; final review OWN-13) once it holds a value, else the one stored for the campaign path,
else 404 (the page then says the values are filled in on Inputs). An assembled CPF that holds no value yet is not
answered in place of the stored one, nor as an empty table (round 3: a project whose inputs had assembled nothing
answered 200 with no parameter where it answered 404).

Where this project's client files may be sent for an AI model to read: in-house only unless a cloud service has
the client's recorded permission; whether the reader may change it (its owner or an administrator).

put.description:
Record where this project's client files may go, as a whole: in-house only, or the cloud services the client
allowed, each with the client's written permission (its reference) and when it ends. Only the project's owner or an
administrator (403 `NOT_OWNER_OR_ADMIN`). Confirmed with the step-up and audited; the agents follow it from their
next request.

get.description:
The whole Data room: files, the question, every section's values with their sources and statuses, the
decisions, data requests, simulation plan and PK-Sim inputs.

post.description: Choose one of a decision's options, with the reason (a choice other than the suggestion needs one).
A value entered by a person, recorded as Entered with the reason.

get.description: A delivered file as the source viewer opens it: its pages with their size in points, or its parts of lines.

One page of a delivered file drawn as it was read: the reading copy (a PDF turned upright, an image as a scan)
made again from the file's bytes, so a chip's box falls where it is drawn.
One part of a delivered file (a sheet, a Word or text body, a page's lines), numbered as the agents read it.

post.description:
An existing project's client files, as the earlier Inputs page recorded them, added as the Data room's uploads,
each once (plan §4: "Open in the Data room" reads their stored files again). Run reads them.

get.description:
What "Send to the model" would send now (evidence items and observed datasets) and what blocks it; nothing is
written.

post.description:
Send the room's confirmed inputs to the model: compound and release values as accepted evidence, each arm's mean
profile as an accepted observed dataset, so Review & sign starts from them. Signed with the token's recent step-up
(403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`); refused (409 with every reason, nothing signed) while anything blocks it. Sending again
adds only what changed.

put.description: The question card as the modeler confirms or edits it (a confirmation is audited with its checklist).

patch.description: A data request's wording to the client, or its status (open, not needed for this question, answered).

post.description:
Run the Data room in the background: the files read (OCR included), then the agents that have a model. Each
stage's answers are kept per file, so a second run redoes only what is new, unless `redo` names the stage.

Store the client's delivery as it came: many files, a zip, or both (an archive is unpacked when the files are
read). A file sent twice is stored once.

The manual path for observed data (typed from a table or a report). Its origin says what it is: synthetic or
illustrative data are accepted for software checks but can never pass a gate (plan §9.4).
A blinded dataset's values for one check (digitization, acceptance), with the reason on the audit chain.

A study's facts: the multiple-dose regimen, the demographics or the explicit healthy adult default (D-29), with
no reason asked (D-27; the audit keeps before and after). The inputs are assembled again.
A figure digitized by a person: the server maps the picked pixels with the calibration (no client arithmetic).

get.description:
The Delivery section's page: every delivery with its files and their coverage, the subjects to review, the
"study not stated" values, the mappings that wait and the client request. Looking at it queues the client files
stored before the pipeline ran and starts the intake job when a run waits. Poll while `running`.

A mapping as a person reviews it: each column's header with its role, field and unit, the tokens and row rules,
a table of its layout (no digit of its body), every version with its decisions, where it is in use, and how the
version shown reads each table in use (`tables`). `version`: one version (default: the latest). `file_sha256` and
`region_id` (both or neither): the table to show it on, the one a person opened it from (409 when that region is
no table of this layout).

post.description:
A person's approval of one version: the values read under it become `approved_mapping`, the version governs
its layout from now on, and the files that hold such a table are read again.

Store a person's version of the mapping (checked by code on its table: a spec with an error is refused, 422
with the findings) and read the files that hold such a table again. It waits for approval like any version.

A person's rejection of one version, with why: it is never read with again, and the files that hold such a
table are read again. Until that run is done the table shows as waiting (its earlier values are still active).

A person's layout for one table, which needs no mapping to exist yet: the first layout of a table no version
reads (unread, or its reading rejected), or a new version of its layout's mapping. The spec is checked by code on
that table (422 `MAPPING_INVALID` with the findings), stored as a person's version of the mapping of the table's
layout fingerprint (audited `intake.mapping.propose`), and the files that hold a table of that layout are read
again. It waits for approval like any version. 409: the table's source model is not cached, the region is no
table, or the spec is a version a person rejected.

A person's decision that regions of a file are not data (scope `regions`: any region, and what was read from
it is set aside; `unread_prose`; `figures`), or that items outside every region are not (`outside`: their
locators). The file's coverage is recomputed. 409 `CONFLICT` for one a person's decision sets aside already
(restore it to decide again), with who decided, when and why (`detail.decided`: where, by, at, why, the why masked
for a file that holds a blinded study's values); nothing is written then.

Undo a person's "not data" decision, with the reason: an appended line that names the decisions it undoes,
every one in force on what it lists (the earlier lines stay, audited `intake.region.restore`). What they set aside counts again: the values read from those
regions are proposed again and the file's coverage is recomputed. 409 `CONFLICT` when one listed is not marked as
not data by a person (nothing to restore); nothing is written then. A region excluded before its outcome was kept
is read again (its file is queued).

get.description:
What the review shows beside a value: its table with the value's cell and its time, unit and label cells
highlighted by role, or its paragraph with the span marked. Give `value` (a value's id) or `anchor` (an anchor
text), one of them.

A subject's card, exceptions first: its blockers, schema gaps, checks, conflicts, cross-file links, missing
items and new mappings; then its values by table, what the landing would hold back, the spot check's state and
its confirmation with the signature's manifestation.

What confirming the subject now would change, before anything is signed (the console redesign's slice 4c): the
datasets and evidence its landing would load, revise, accept or set aside, the dissolution rows it would load and
remove, and every artifact downstream that would go stale (a signed MAP must then be signed again). The landing is
planned as `:confirm` plans it; nothing is signed or written. Refused for a blinded study (409 BLINDED: what it
would load names its values) and while the landing cannot be planned (409 LANDING_REFUSED).

The subject's latest spot check as it stands: its draw, its record and each value drawn, read only. Showing a
recorded spot check again draws nothing (a draw is written only by `:draw`, and once its ticks are recorded a draw
asked again is a new one); a blinded study's values are withheld as everywhere.

post.description:
Every tick of a draw, once, in one request: a tick says the value, its unit, its time, its labels and its
statistic match the source.

Draw the subject's spot check from the ledger's state (the same state gives the same draw): each value with the
tuple it is ticked for and its source reference. A blinded study's cannot be drawn (409 `BLINDED`).
Settle an open conflict of the subject: the value kept stays, the others that read differently are excluded.

Confirm the subject: sign the record that binds its values, its decisions, its spot check and its coverage, and
land it in the project. Refused (409, with every blocker; nothing is signed) while anything blocks it. Needs a
fresh step-up (403 `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`). An interrupted landing completes here with no new signature.
A requirement item of the subject that is missing: ask the client, take it from literature, or not needed.

A person's entry or correction of a value of the subject, with the reason (method "person": no source, the
confirmation's signature binds it). The facts code derives from it follow.

Confirm or refuse a cross-file link of the study, per file; for an ambiguous link, `study` is the candidate
chosen (the file's own study is merged into it).

Clear a failed check of the subject with a reason. A missing required item is settled by a disposition and an
open conflict by a choice, never by an override.

Give "study not stated" values their subject: a study (and its arm), a product (and its batch), or both, and
their analyte when stated. A study, a product, an arm, a batch or an analyte no file's label gave an entity is
named here (`new_study`, `new_product`, `new_arm`, `new_batch`, `new_analyte`): it is created, never as a duplicate
of one that exists (409, naming it; an arm inside its study, a batch inside its product), and the values are
assigned to it.

get.description:
The words a table's layout (`mapping/2`) is written with, as every mapping answer gives them (`vocabulary`,
read from `modeler_intake.mapping_spec` and `fields`), for a project where no table has a layout yet: the form
that gives a table its first layout offers these and never makes one up. 409 while the pipeline is off.

post.description:
Read files again (all of them, or the ones named by sha256): each is queued as a new run, behind the runs that
wait. "RUNNING" when the intake job runs now, "QUEUED" when the runs wait for it.

Propose a profile's fit as a formulation's release model: evidence to accept or reject on the Parameters tab
(which profile represents in vivo release is a planning decision, D-12).

Store documents in the project's library. `step` and `task`: what they relate to (the "Add data" card). `read`:
also read each one for data (plan 2026-11-10, R2; "Add data" asks for it by default): a PDF, Word file or workbook
added as an annex, context, paper or other document is read by code and queued for the reading agent, its role
kept; `reading` names the files queued, `not_read` the ones that are not, with why.

get.description:
The images placed in a PDF, page by page, where each sits (the digitizer crops the page to one); [] for a file
that is not a PDF.

The stored file itself. A file that holds a blinded study's values (`blinded_sources`, D-15) is not served until
the MAP is signed: 409 BLINDED (final review INT-3). Its pages are read masked (`pages/{n}`); a blinded dataset is
seen for a check through `datasets/{id}:reveal`, with a reason on the audit chain, which gives its values, never the
file.

post.description: Put a withdrawn document back in use, with a reason.

Set or change a client file's tag (plan 2026-11-03 §3.1, option D: editable at any time). It settles an open
proposal: used when the person took the proposed kind, kept otherwise. No reason is asked.

Withdraw a document with a reason (the owner's answer 12): never erased, marked in the library, hidden from the
agents. The values already taken from it keep their citation; a person rejects them on Inputs if they must go.

Read for data every document a person added to the library that was never read (an annex added before "Read for
data" existed, say): each becomes a client file too, read by code and queued for the reading agent.
The manual path: a person enters a value with its source. A quote from a stored document is checked verbatim.
Keep this value for its parameter: the other accepted values of the same target are rejected with the reason.

Correct the parameter a value is for, or its conditions: a corrected copy replaces it (the original is kept,
rejected, pointing at the copy).

A published OSP model of the project's drug as a source (redesign §5, in place of the Quick start wizard): its
values are proposed citing the model and its clinical datasets citing their publications; they flow in like any
other source and rank below the client and the literature (D-32). A model of another drug is refused.

Run the structured sources then A2 (values) or, with ``?agent=A3``, the observed-data agent, in the background.
With agents off, the structured sources alone (code, no AI; plan 2026-11-05 §3.3).
What saving `content` as the next version of `kind/id` would change and make stale. Saves nothing.

put.description: A structure choice with its reason; the inputs are re-assembled with it.

post.description: Propose the molecular weight from the brief's PubChem record (accepted like any other evidence).

get.description: The project's document library (plan 2026-10-28, PR 1): every document with who added it and what cites it.

Where the literature agent stands, for the Inputs page to show its progress while it searches (plan 2026-11-05
§3.3), in place of "already running". Small, so the page can ask every few seconds.

post.description: An MS-01 candidate kept fixed: the diagnosis does not fit it within MS-01's default (D-37).
A held candidate back to MS-01's default: the diagnosis may fit it again (D-37).
The person's fit taken back: the parameter is fixed again, or an MS-01 candidate within MS-01's default (D-37).

put.description:
Estimated parameters fitted as one, through one factor (PI-4 B2): each at f x its start value, so their split
is kept. Why, and where the split comes from, are required and signed with the MAP.

post.description: A group taken back: its members are fitted each on its own again.

put.description: A study dropped on a D3 node: placed by a person (userLocked), with the reason. ``dry_run`` validates only.

post.description:
A study a person placed, given back to the MS-01 default ("Back to the MS-01 default" on Review & sign). ``dry_run``
says what it would change (the validator, the diff, whether it is a MAP deviation) and saves nothing.

put.description: A structure choice; the default split depends on some of them, so non-locked placements follow the new default.

post.description:
New inputs (P4 changed) or a brief edit: the default is recomputed and the structure read again from the brief,
a person's choices are kept, new studies are marked.
Approve and sign: the MAP generated from the plan, signed (Part 11, step-up), and the campaign inputs staged.

get.description: Read-only view for viewers (the plan must exist).

post.description: Stage the CPF, generate + persist the MAP, and derive observed PK, returning the runner's inputs.

get.description:
The reading tray (plan 2026-11-10, R3): every client file queued for the reading agent, being read, read or
failed, with what was found and why one failed. Like the client-data page, looking at it queues a file never queued
and starts the reading when files wait and none runs.

post.description:
Read a file of the tray again (one that failed, or one read before): queued behind the others. "RUNNING" when
the reading starts now, "QUEUED" when it waits (or agents are off: it is read once they are on).

put.description: A person's decision on one item (who provides it, for what, cross-check it) — kept across re-derivations.

get.description:
The signatures given on this project's records (R-N09), newest first: every `signature.create` event of the
company's audit chain whose record is the project's (its id starts with the project's: an intake confirmation, the
MAP and its deviations, the Data room's publication) or a decision on one of its campaigns' escalations (signed as
"{campaign_id}-{stage}"), which the project's audit trail, filtered by the project's prefix, does not list.

What was made from inputs that have since changed, with why. Where a project stands is its steps (below), read
from what is filled and missing, never from approvals (D-27).

Start, Inputs, Review & sign and Run, each done, waiting on the person, running or not started, from what is
filled and what is missing (the redesign, D-27), never from an approval.

The observed clinical studies of this project (what a campaign fits and validates against): those uploaded for the
campaign path, then the studies of the catalog Inputs assembles (what a signed plan stages; final review OWN-13: the
Run page listed none while Inputs had a study in the model), each once, an upload first.

post.description: Add observed studies to the project, replacing any with the same ``study_id`` and keeping the rest.

get.description:
The project's model system (compounds and roles, formation, products with their dose fractions, analytes and
the stages that judge each, MS-01 v1.3 §6.5), or none for a single-compound project.

put.description:
Relate the project's compounds as one model system (parent, enantiomers, metabolites): roles, formation links,
products with their dose fractions (required: never defaulted), published sum observers and analytes. Each
compound's CPF is put first; the system is checked against them before it is stored.

get.description:
The person's other projects of the same drug and what each found that this project does not hold yet (plan
2026-11-05 §3.3): literature and public-source values only.

post.description:
Reuse here, with the person's consent (this call), the values another project of the same drug found: each
proposed anew with its source and quote, its document copied, to decide like any value.

P0: create the project from the drug name, the technical proposal and the client's files (one upload, map rows
p0-files and p3-upload), then start the extraction. A client file that cannot be read is answered with the reason;
the project still starts. `tags`: what each client file is, per file name (plan 2026-11-03 §3.1); each answer says
the tag kept and any other tag code read from the file's content.

get.description: Pending agent parameter proposals awaiting curator acceptance (review inbox).

get.description: The wizard's starting points, the published real-data model first.
One starting point in full: the CPF, the studies in the upload shape, and what was left out and why.
